text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: 🔔 P1 - auth-service: token validation error spike (kid mismatch) — PD-47322. Paging auth on-call now.

pagerduty: Alert triggered (PD-47322) — 5xx on /v1/auth/validate, error rate 18% over 5m.

devon: acked. I’m on it, grabbing logs and JWKS.

samira: ack — at lunch but reachable. if you need escalation ping kevin.

devon: quick snapshot: signs in logs: 
```
ERR jwt_validation: jwt signature failed, kid not found: kid=kp_2026_09
WARN jwks_fetch: cached keys last_refresh=12h
```
looks like signing key rotated but JWKS cache not refreshed.

ops-bot: Current traffic impact: 12% of auth validations failing globally, spike concentrated in us-east-1.

samira: customers affected: a subset of API requests for real-time embeds and token-exchange flows. Called out customers: acme-analytics, tiltops, and a few sandbox orgs.

devon: I’m going to flush local JWKS caches on the fleet and force re-fetch on the edge. Doing canary first.

devon: running command to trigger JWKS refresh on canary nodes: `for n in canary-list; do curl -X POST http://$n/internal/keys/refresh; done`

devon: canary refresh succeeded, validation errors dropped to 1.5% on canary. Rolling to us-east-1 next.

kevin: if this is from a key rotation, we should fallback to old signing service until JWKS propagates. Can we enable legacy key acceptance briefly?

devon: we have a fallback path but it's disabled by default. toggling now: `/api/feature-flags/auth-legacy-key-accept true`

samira: hold on legacy accept — if we enable, we need to ensure audit events mark fallback. ok from security side as temporary if limited to 30m. :lock:

devon: legacy accept on for us-east-1. error rate dropped to 0.8% and customer errors trending down.

pagerduty: Acknowledgment recorded by devon at 2178901241.

ops-bot: Canary -> us-east rollout completed (12 nodes updated). Global error rate now 0.9%.

kevin: good. next steps: 1) coordinate with key management to confirm rotation details 2) schedule automated JWKS refresh on rotate 3) plan a postmortem.

samira: I’ll own the customer comms draft. Quick blurb: "We experienced a short-lived authentication error due to key propagation delay. Temporary mitigation applied; no user data exposed." Will share draft in #customer-commms.

devon: notes for ops: observed root cause = key rotated in signing service (kp_2026_09) but edge JWKS cache TTL prevented immediate propagation. Some tokens signed with new kid while validators still used cached set.

kevin: action items:
- devon: implement aggressive refresh on detection (15m) and add metric for jwks_mismatch_count
- infra: add webhook from signing service to edge to invalidate caches on rotate
- product/security: confirm acceptable fallback policy window and audit log format

devon: adding quick log snippet I used to detect kid mismatch: `grep -i "kid not found" /var/log/auth/*.log | tail -n 50`

samira: handing off on-call to kevin — had to step out for 20m. context pinned above. kevin, please take ownership for now. :handshake:

kevin: taking over on-call. devon, keep me posted if anything re-escalates. I’ll join the postmortem sync in 30m.

devon: left a temp tag on the signing service: `rollback-accept-legacy` until 2026-09-15T14:30Z. Will revert as soon as JWKS propagation confirmed.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-09-AuthKeyPropagation. Priority P1. Link: https://incidents.example.com/INC-2026-09-AuthKeyPropagation

samira: customer comms draft posted: https://docs.internal/customer-comms/auth-2026-09-draft (please review).

kevin: launching postmortem template now and assigning owners. tagging product, infra, security.

devon: final status for now: mitigation in place, legacy accept enabled for 20m window, JWKS refresh queued and verified. Monitoring for 30m before close.

kevin: thanks — if error rate creeps above 2% re-alert and I’ll escalate to ENG-SRE.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: PD-47322 marked as resolved by devon at 2178901447 (ack + mitigation).

devon: closing thread for timeline. will follow up with postmortem and action items.

kevin: copied. good job team. :tada:
